div.l: Of Norfolk was the Reve of which I telle
Beside a toun̄ men̄ calle it Baldiswelle
Tuckid he was as is a frere about
And euer he rode the hynderst of oure rout
A Somonour ther was with us in þat place
That had a fire rede cherubins face ·
For sauceflume was he with eyen narow ·
And hoot he was and lecherous as a Sparow
With scallid browis and pillid berd
Of his visage children were afferd
Ther nas quiksiluer litarge ne brymstone ·
Borage Corus nor oyle of tartre none
Ne oynement that wold clense and bite
That him might helpe of his whelkis white
Nor of the cnobbis sitting on his chekis
Wel loued he garlik oynons and eke lekis
And forto drink strong wine reed as blood
Than wold he speke and crie as he were wood
And whan he had wel drunken the wine
Than wold he no wurd speke but latine
A few termes he had two or thre ·
That he had lerned of sum decre
No wundir is he herd it al the day
And eke ye know wel hough that a Iay
Can clepe watte as wel as the pope .
But whoso couth in othir thingis him grope
Than had he spent alle his philosophie
Ay questio quid iuris wold he crie
He was a gentil harlot and a kynde
A bettir felow shuld men none finde
He wold suffre for a quart of wine
A good felou to haue his concubine
A . xij . month / ⁊and excuse him atte fulle
Ful priuely a fynche eke couth he pulle
And if he founde owhere a good felaw
He wold teche him to haue none awe
In such caas of the Archdiacons curse
But if a mannes soule were in his purse
For in his purse he shuld y punysshid be ·
Curse is the Archdiacons helle seid he
But wel I wote he lyed right in dede
Of cursing ought eche gilty man̄ to drede
